jobs.description:
**Software Engineer, Infrastructure**
=====================================

**Hybrid in Palo Alto (Mon / Wed / Thurs) · $185K–$215K base + meaningful early-stage equity + full benefits**

**About Sodalis**
-----------------

Specialty pharmacy is where the most complex and expensive drugs reach the most in-need patients, and it still runs on faxes, phone tag, and manual data entry. Patients wait weeks for therapies that can't wait.

Sodalis is building AI agents that run those operations end to end: reading and validating prescriptions, handling phone calls, and moving prescriptions through eligibility and fulfillment. The ambition goes beyond that. We want to be the rails every specialty prescription runs on, and the first system to perform clinical review at the standard of a pharmacist.

We're already in production, processing tens of thousands of prescriptions a week. Backed by Gradient Ventures (Google's AI fund), and founded by veterans of Apple's Applied ML, Included Health, and Avella Specialty Pharmacy (scaled to $1.5B+ before its acquisition by OptumRx).

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

Everything we run today is cloud-based, and so are the pharmacy management systems we integrate with. But most of the specialty pharmacy market runs on-prem. To reach it, our system has to run on the pharmacy's systems instead of ours. Whether that's the full stack on-site or a hybrid split with our cloud is one of the first decisions you'd make. That's the problem you'd own.  
We've never shipped an on-prem deployment, so there's no pattern to follow. You'll decide how our architecture gets packaged and deployed into environments we don't control, what has to change in our current infrastructure to make that possible, and how we maintain and see into those deployments once they're live.

We don't yet know what these environments look like in detail. Some pharmacies may have restricted outbound access, legacy hardware, or IT teams that can't give us a login; others may be more open. Part of the job is going in with our customer, finding out what's actually there, and designing something that works across the range.  
You'll start with our AI pharmacy tech product, rolling out with a committed customer, so you build against a real deployment instead of a hypothetical one. You'd work directly with the founders and the early engineering team on the architecture.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Decide how our architecture runs in a pharmacy's environment, starting with the AI pharmacy tech product: full stack on-site, a hybrid split with our cloud, or something in between.
* Adapt our current infrastructure and build the packaging and deployment path that installs and updates Sodalis at each pharmacy.
* Own those deployments over time: upgrades, rollbacks, and observability into health and failures without being on site.
* Go in with our customer and pharmacy IT teams to learn what their environments actually allow, and design for the range.
* Partner with the founders and early engineering team on architecture.

**What we're looking for**
--------------------------

* 5+ years in infrastructure or platform engineering.
* You've taken an AWS-native stack and made it run on Kubernetes or similar in environments you don't operate, including stateful services.
* You've shipped and maintained software running in environments you don't control: on-prem, customer-hosted, edge, or embedded.
* You've kept a fleet of remote installs updated, observable, and recoverable without being able to log into them.
* You've set the first pattern for something in a startup and are comfortable with ambiguity.
* You'll spend time with pharmacy IT teams and need to understand their constraints firsthand. No healthcare background required.

**How we work**
---------------

We're a handful of people going all in on a problem we think is worth it, holding a high bar and shipping work that reaches real patients. It's intense, and it isn't for everyone. We want people who want to build something that matters, alongside others who care as much as they do. If that's you, we should talk.

Compensation Range: $185K - $215K

Responsibilities
  
  
The TikTok Privacy and Security (PnS) R&D team creates privacy solutions that are intuitive for users, auditable for regulators, and sustainable for the company, making TikTok a platform where people can safely discover, create, and connect. We build user-facing privacy features, including privacy settings, consent management, data access and export, and age-appropriate experiences. We protect personal data across its full lifecycle, from collection and transfer through access, storage, retention, and deletion. We develop the platforms, technical controls, and governance tools behind privacy protection and regulatory compliance in global markets, and we bring privacy-enhancing technologies and research into production at scale. We tackle challenges unique to operating a platform at global scale: translating rapidly evolving laws and policies into reliable technical controls, providing transparency and auditability across highly complex data systems, supporting different regulatory requirements across regions, and making privacy protection work at the quality and speed production systems demand. You will work across product privacy, data lifecycle management, data protection and residency, privacy engineering platforms, AI governance, and privacy-preserving technologies, using techniques including automated compliance enforcement, data lineage and taxonomy, differential privacy, trusted execution environments, AI fairness, and privacy protection for generative AI. The systems you build will protect hundreds of millions of people, and the privacy decisions you make will reach every one of them. TikTok's Privacy and Security (PNS) Data Retention team makes sure that data across the platform is kept only as long as it is needed, and is then deleted reliably and verifiably. The data covers online services, offline warehouses, logs, backups, and ML training datasets. Global privacy rules keep getting stricter, and the data estate keeps growing to exabyte scale. The team owns the policies, platforms, and technical controls that turn retention commitments into guarantees we can enforce and audit. As a Backend Engineer - Data Retention, you will design and build scalable, reliable, high-performance systems that manage the lifecycle of data at TikTok scale. That includes finding and classifying data, applying retention policies, running deletion, and proving that deletion happened. You will turn fast-changing privacy and regulatory requirements into concrete platform capabilities. You will work closely with storage infrastructure, data platform, ML platform, product, privacy, legal, and security teams to ship solutions across thousands of services and storage systems. Responsibilities: - Design and build large-scale data lifecycle management systems that enforce retention policies across heterogeneous storage: RDBMS, KV stores, caches, message queues, data warehouses (Hive/HDFS), object storage, logs, and backups. - Build and run high-throughput deletion pipelines, such as TTL enforcement, user account deletion propagation, and partition and snapshot expiry. They must be correct, idempotent, and observable, and must not hurt the stability or performance of production systems. - Build data discovery and inventory capabilities, including metadata collection, data lineage, and classification of personal and sensitive data. These keep retention policies accurately mapped to real storage assets. - Build verification, auditing, and reporting systems that prove deletion is complete and on time. Provide evidence for internal audits and regulator inquiries. - Support exception workflows such as legal holds, retention extensions, and policy approvals, with fine-grained access control and full audit trails. - Work with ML platform teams to extend retention and deletion controls to training datasets, feature stores, and derived artifacts such as embeddings and model checkpoints. - Work with privacy, legal, and compliance teams so that systems meet applicable regulations (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and other global and regional privacy laws) and TikTok's own data commitments. - Help shape the technical roadmap for the data retention platform, and find and evaluate new techniques and tools that improve coverage, efficiency, and reliability at scale.
  
  
Qualifications
  
  
Minimum Qualifications - Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field. - 3+ years of backend development experience in Go, Java, C++, or Python. - Strong background in large-scale distributed systems, databases, messaging and streaming systems (such as Kafka or Flink), and caching. - Solid understanding of storage internals and data lifecycle concepts, such as TTL, compaction, partitioning, snapshots and backups, and consistency models. - Experience building high-throughput batch or streaming data pipelines with strong correctness guarantees (idempotency, retries, exactly-once or at-least-once semantics). - Experience with microservices architecture and containerization (Docker, Kubernetes). - Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS or GCP and experience with Agile development and DevOps practices. - Strong communication and collaboration skills, and the ability to work independently and drive cross-team projects across multiple priorities. Preferred Qualifications - 5+ years of industry experience, with significant time on storage infrastructure, data platforms, or privacy and data governance systems. - Hands-on experience with data retention, data deletion, data inventory and classification, or data lineage systems at large internet scale. - Familiarity with privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA) and industry standards (ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, NIST Privacy Framework). - Experience with big data ecosy

**About us**  
  
  

One team. Global challenges. Infinite opportunities. At Viasat, we’re on a mission to deliver connections with the capacity to change the world. **What you'll do**  
  
  

As a Senior Systems Engineer on the ACT team, you’ll turn early ideas into working prototypes — spanning satellite communications, PNT, and related systems — to test technical and operational hypotheses. You’ll own the front-end analysis — trade studies, feasibility assessments, and system architecture — that shapes what we build, and you’ll produce the clear artifacts that let a concept move forward for execution at scale. As the team’s senior systems engineer, you’ll be the technical anchor for the system model — driving how it’s structured and built, guiding the engineers doing the hands-on build, and keeping architecture, interfaces, and analysis coherent as prototypes evolve. This is a fast-paced, integrative role focused on prototyping, not production hardening.

  
  
**The day-to-day**  
  
  

* Run trade studies and feasibility analysis to compare concepts and recommend an approach.
* Develop system and subsystem concepts and architectures, and define interfaces (ICDs) across RF, digital, software, and timing — including for components sourced from different groups, aligned to representative open-architecture interfaces.
* Model and analyze system performance in MATLAB and/or Python (for example, link budgets, RF cascades, and error budgets).
* Perform quantitative modeling and analysis of signal, propagation, and geometry effects to support PNT, signals-of-opportunity, and communications concepts.
* Produce clean specifications, models, and hand-off artifacts so prototypes can transition for build-out at scale.
* Work closely across signal processing, embedded, FPGA, software, and integration & test to keep the integrated system coherent and performing — supporting prototype bring-up and testing, and keeping the system model current as the design evolves.

* Working knowledge of RF, SATCOM/communications, or PNT domains.
* Strong written and verbal communication, including clear diagrams and documentation.

* Familiarity with SATCOM terminals or satellite communications networks, and how positioning, navigation, and timing services ride on them.

**Software Engineer, Infrastructure**
=====================================

**Hybrid in Palo Alto (Mon / Wed / Thurs) · $185K–$215K base + meaningful early-stage equity + full benefits**

**About Sodalis**
-----------------

Specialty pharmacy is where the most complex and expensive drugs reach the most in-need patients, and it still runs on faxes, phone tag, and manual data entry. Patients wait weeks for therapies that can't wait.

Sodalis is building AI agents that run those operations end to end: reading and validating prescriptions, handling phone calls, and moving prescriptions through eligibility and fulfillment. The ambition goes beyond that. We want to be the rails every specialty prescription runs on, and the first system to perform clinical review at the standard of a pharmacist.

We're already in production, processing tens of thousands of prescriptions a week. Backed by Gradient Ventures (Google's AI fund), and founded by veterans of Apple's Applied ML, Included Health, and Avella Specialty Pharmacy (scaled to $1.5B+ before its acquisition by OptumRx).

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

Everything we run today is cloud-based, and so are the pharmacy management systems we integrate with. But most of the specialty pharmacy market runs on-prem. To reach it, our system has to run on the pharmacy's systems instead of ours. Whether that's the full stack on-site or a hybrid split with our cloud is one of the first decisions you'd make. That's the problem you'd own.  
We've never shipped an on-prem deployment, so there's no pattern to follow. You'll decide how our architecture gets packaged and deployed into environments we don't control, what has to change in our current infrastructure to make that possible, and how we maintain and see into those deployments once they're live.

We don't yet know what these environments look like in detail. Some pharmacies may have restricted outbound access, legacy hardware, or IT teams that can't give us a login; others may be more open. Part of the job is going in with our customer, finding out what's actually there, and designing something that works across the range.  
You'll start with our AI pharmacy tech product, rolling out with a committed customer, so you build against a real deployment instead of a hypothetical one. You'd work directly with the founders and the early engineering team on the architecture.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Decide how our architecture runs in a pharmacy's environment, starting with the AI pharmacy tech product: full stack on-site, a hybrid split with our cloud, or something in between.
* Adapt our current infrastructure and build the packaging and deployment path that installs and updates Sodalis at each pharmacy.
* Own those deployments over time: upgrades, rollbacks, and observability into health and failures without being on site.
* Go in with our customer and pharmacy IT teams to learn what their environments actually allow, and design for the range.
* Partner with the founders and early engineering team on architecture.

**What we're looking for**
--------------------------

* 5+ years in infrastructure or platform engineering.
* You've taken an AWS-native stack and made it run on Kubernetes or similar in environments you don't operate, including stateful services.
* You've shipped and maintained software running in environments you don't control: on-prem, customer-hosted, edge, or embedded.
* You've kept a fleet of remote installs updated, observable, and recoverable without being able to log into them.
* You've set the first pattern for something in a startup and are comfortable with ambiguity.
* You'll spend time with pharmacy IT teams and need to understand their constraints firsthand. No healthcare background required.

**How we work**
---------------

We're a handful of people going all in on a problem we think is worth it, holding a high bar and shipping work that reaches real patients. It's intense, and it isn't for everyone. We want people who want to build something that matters, alongside others who care as much as they do. If that's you, we should talk.

Compensation Range: $185K - $215K
